newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: RUGBY UNION-INJURED EALES SETS SIGHTS ON WELSH TEST.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-INJURED EALES SETS SIGHTS ON WELSH TEST.

text.p: Wallaby captain John Eales should be available for next weekend's test against Wales despite suffering an eye injury in his side's hard-fought 22-12 win over Ireland on Saturday.
Eales was forced off midway through the second-half with his side trailing 12-9. Although tests revealed a bruised cornea, he should be available for the Welsh encounter.
"All things going well, he'll be back for next week. We expect him to regain full sight later today," said team manager Peter Falk.
Wallaby coach Greg Smith paid tribute to the Irish effort and praised his own side's resilience.
"It's a terrific win, but full credit to the Irish for the way they played. It was just the type of game we expected it to be."

Irish full-back Jim Staples faces a lengthy lay-off after breaking a bone in his wrist, but coach Murray Kidd was encouraged by the display of a team which contained only six survivors from the side who lost to Western Samoa last week.
"It's certainly a huge improvement, but when you get that close you want to get a result out of it. We did make one or two mistakes we have to eradicate."
